trials.name: FINGER
trials.drug: Multi-domain lifestyle intervention (nutrition, exercise, cognitive training, vascular monitoring)
trials.sponsor: Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare
trials.population: Adults aged 60-77 years with elevated dementia risk (CAIDE score >= 6) and cognition at or slightly below average for age
trials.primary_endpoint: Cognitive impairment assessed with a Neuropsychological Test Battery (NTB), and Stroop and Trail Making tests over 2 years
trials.results_summary: At 2 years, the multidomain intervention significantly improved cognitive functioning compared to the control group (between-group difference in NTB total Z score change of 0.022 per year, p=0.030).

trials.name: US-POINTER
trials.population: Adults aged 60-79 years at risk of cognitive decline with a sedentary lifestyle and suboptimal diet
trials.results_summary: A structured multidomain intervention produced a statistically significant, greater improvement in global cognition over 2 years compared to an unstructured, self-guided intervention (difference of 0.029 SD/year, p=0.008).

trials.name: MET-FINGER
trials.population: Older adults at risk for dementia
trials.primary_endpoint: Change in cognition, unit on a scale

related_evidence.description: Primary 2-year results of the FINGER trial in The Lancet, demonstrating significant cognitive benefits of the multidomain intervention.
Primary results of the US-POINTER trial in JAMA, demonstrating that structured lifestyle interventions significantly improve global cognition.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence supporting the central claim—that a multi-domain lifestyle intervention can reduce cognitive decline—is robust, highly influential, and successfully replicated. The original FINGER trial provided landmark proof-of-concept in 2015, demonstrating that combining nutritional guidance, physical exercise, cognitive training, and vascular risk monitoring significantly preserved cognitive function in at-risk older adults over two years. This breakthrough inspired the World-Wide FINGERS network, leading directly to replications like the US-POINTER trial, which confirmed in August 2025 that structured lifestyle interventions improve global cognition more than self-guided approaches. Ongoing studies, such as the MET-FINGER trial, are actively investigating whether layering pharmacological treatments like metformin onto these established lifestyle modifications can yield even greater neuroprotective benefits.
discrepancies: The document correctly notes that no empirical data or results are posted directly on the ClinicalTrials.gov registry for NCT01041989 and that its status is listed as 'UNKNOWN'; however, this reflects poor registry maintenance rather than a lack of actual data, as the study's highly successful primary outcomes were peer-reviewed and published in The Lancet in 2015.
